Vertical Atmospheric Mode Decomposition¶

class safe_vamd.vamdecomp.VAMDecomp(acoustic_field=None, x_samples=None, z_samples=None, p_samples=None)¶

Bases: object

Represents an application of Vertical-Atmospheric Mode-Decomposition (VAMD).

Class attributes:

acoustic_field¶

An instance of AcousticField with the Vertical Atmospheric (VA) mode basis.

Type:

AcousticField

An instance of ModeFilter with methods capable of filtering the original VA mode basis.

ModeFilter

load_samples_from_txt(sample_path)¶

Loads the acoustic samples from a semicolon separated .txt file with a header followed by columns for, respectively, height (in \(m\)), range (in \(m\)), real part (in \(Pa\), or unitless) and imaginary part (in \(Pa\), or unitless).

Parameters:

sample_path (str) – The path to the .txt file containing the acoustic samples (pressure or transfer functions).

Return type:

None

load_modes_from_txt(downwind_path=None, upwind_path=None)¶

Receives the path to .txt file(s) with the downwind, upwind or both set(s) of modes, creates an instance of AcousticField, defines it as an attribute of VAMDecomp and uses its load_modes_from_txt method to load the VA modes.

For a mode basis with eigenvectors of size \(N\) and \(K\) number of VA modes, the .txt file for each mode basis should have the following format:

\[\begin{split}\begin{matrix} z_1 & p_1(z_1) & \dots & p_K(z_1) \\ \dots & \dots & \dots & \dots \\ z_N & p_1(z_N) & \dots & p_K(z_N) \\ \hline \text{#} & A_1 & \dots & A_K \\ \text{#} & \lambda_1 & \dots & \lambda_K \\ \text{#} & k^{ref}_1 & \dots & k^{ref}_K \end{matrix}\end{split}\]

, where \(p_i(z_j)\) represents the shape at height \((z_j)\), \(A_i\) the amplitude, \(\lambda_i\) the eigenvalue, and \(k^{ref}_i\) the reference wavenumber for mode i. The symbol # represents irrelevant information in the .txt file.

Parameters:

  • downwind_path (str, optional) – The path to the .txt file with the downwind VA modes.

  • upwind_path (str, optional) – The path to the .txt file with the upwind VA modes.

Return type:

None

match_modes_to_samples(side='downwind', spread_3d=False, condition_monitor=False)¶

Sets a regression problem (\(P \simeq M^{'} \cdot A^{'}\)) between the acoustic samples \(P\) and a linear combination of the VA mode basis, represented by \(M^{'} \cdot A^{'}\), and computes the least-squares solution (see Section 2.4 in https://doi.org/10.1016/j.enganabound.2025.106308). The problem is set up on an auxiliary coordinate system \((x' = x - x_{\text{ref}}, z' = z)\), best defined near the sampling positions \((x_j, z_j)\) to improve conditioning. The auxiliary coord. system has its origin at \(x_{ref}\). The modal amplitudes computed at the auxiliary referential are then converted into the original coordinate system (\(A = E \cdot A^{'}\)).

Parameters:

  • side (str, optional) – Which mode basis should be used in the mode decomposition (side = “downwind” makes the procedure use the downwind mode basis, side=”upwind” sets it to use the upwind modes).

  • spread_3d (bool, optional) – Toggles the use of a correction factor accounting for spherical spreading when decomposing into the modes.

  • condition_monitor (bool, optional) – Toggles the computation (and return) of a condition number for the regression problem.

Returns:

Returns only the acoustic field resultant from the mode decomposition or, additionally, the condition number of the pseudo-inverse.

Return type:

AcousticField, tuple[AcousticField, float]

compute_matrix_m(modes, x_ref=0)¶

The individual contributions of the VA modes on the sampling positions, expressed in matrix form.

The contributions are computed in the auxiliary coordinate system \((x' = x - x_{\text{ref}}, z' = z)\), best defined near the sampling positions \((x_j, z_j)\), to improve conditioning.

For \(S\) number of samples and \(K\) number of modes, the method assembles the following matrix:

\[\begin{split}M' = \begin{bmatrix} p_1(z'_1) \cdot e^{-ik_1 x'_1} & \dots & p_K(z'_1) \cdot e^{-ik_K x'_1} \\ \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ p_1(z'_S) \cdot e^{-ik_1 x'_S} & \dots & p_K(z'_S) \cdot e^{-ik_K x'_S} \end{bmatrix}\end{split}\]

where \(p_i(z_j)\) and \(k_i\) are the value of the vertical shape and wave number, respectively, for mode \(i\).

Parameters:

  • modes (Sequence[Mode]) – List of VA modes for which matrix \(M'\) is computed.

  • x_ref (float, optional) – Range origin for the auxiliary coordinate system.

Returns:

Matrix \(M'_{S \times K}\) – a two-dimensional numpy array with the contributions of \(K\) number of VA modes at \(S\) number of sampling locations.

Return type:

NDArray

compute_pseudo_m(modes, x_ref=0, spread_3d=False)¶

Computes the pseudo-inverse of matrix \(M^{'}\) to solve the regression problem (least-squares) \(P \simeq M^{'} \cdot A^{'}\) , where \(S\) number of acoustic samples, expressed by matrix \(P\), are approximated by a linear combination of \(K\) number of VA modes, expressed in matrix form by \(M^{'}\cdot A^{'}\).

Parameters:

  • modes (Sequence[Mode]) – List of modes (instances of Mode) for which the pseudo-inverse matrix is computed.

  • x_ref (float, optional) – Range origin for the auxiliary coordinate system.

  • spread_3d (bool, optional) – Toggles the use of a correction factor \((\sqrt{x \div x_{ref}})^{-1}\) accounting for spherical spreading.

Returns:

Matrix \(M^{-1'}_{K \times S}\) – the pseudo-inverse of matrix \(M^{'}\).

Return type:

np.ndarray

compute_conv_factors(modes, x_ref=0)¶

Computes the conversion diagonal matrix \(E\) for \(K\) number of mode amplitudes (\(A = E \cdot A^{'}\)).

\[\begin{split}E = \begin{bmatrix} e^{ik_1x_{ref}} & 0 & \dots & 0 \\ 0 & e^{ik_2x_{ref}} & \dots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \dots & e^{ik_2x_{ref}} \end{bmatrix}\end{split}\]

, where \(k_i\) is the wavenumber for mode \(i\).

Parameters:

  • modes (Sequence[Mode]) – List of modes (instances of Mode) for which matrix \(E\) is computed.

  • x_ref (float, optional) – Range origin for the auxiliary coordinate system.

Returns:

Matrix \(E_{K \times K}\) - a diagonal matrix with the conversion factors for the modal amplitudes.

Return type:

Sequence[complex]

save_modes_in_txt()¶

saves the mode basis in .txt files with the save_modes_in_txt method in the acoustic_field attribute.

For \(K\) number of VA modes with eigenvectors of size \(N\), the .txt files have the following format:

\[\begin{split}\begin{matrix} z_1 & p_1(z_1) & \dots & p_K(z_1) \\ \dots & \dots & \dots & \dots \\ z_N & p_1(z_N) & \dots & p_K(z_N) \\ \hline \text{#} & A_1 & \dots & A_K \\ \text{#} & \lambda_1 & \dots & \lambda_K \\ \text{#} & k^{ref}_1 & \dots & k^{ref}_K \end{matrix}\end{split}\]

, where \(p_i(z_j)\) represents the vertical shape at height \((z_j)\), \(A_i\) mode amplitude, \(\lambda_i\) the eigenvalue, and \(k^{ref}_i\) the reference wavenumber for mode i. The symbol # represents irrelevant information in the .txt file.

Return type:

None
